I read the plain-words page first, then went and checked it against the record. Most of it is comfortable enough to fit almost any successful public figure: broad-minded, trusted, drawn to learning and advising - that is Macron (philosophy degree, ENA, a run as an economics minister before the presidency), but it is also every senior technocrat anywhere. The favourable list - work and standing, luck and higher study and father, big changes and difficult passages, income and gains - reads true of a man who left investment banking for the fastest presidential rise in the Fifth Republic and is still the head of state, but none of it required knowing his chart; it is the shape any biography of him would produce after the fact.

Where it earns some credit is the one place it says it is stepping outside the ordinary: 'unusually negative about... people who work against you.' Since the botched 2024 snap election, Macron has governed with no majority, burned through several prime ministers, and survived censure motions in a hung parliament - 'rivals working against you' is not a bad label for that stretch, and it is at least a specific, checkable claim rather than a compliment everyone would accept. But the same sentence bundles in 'unusually negative about... debt,' and that part is simply wrong: there is no documented debt trouble in his life, personal or otherwise, and French presidential asset declarations are public. It also calls debt 'live right now' in the same breath it lists money and family life as favourable - the reading wants debt to be both fine and a distinctive sore spot, and reality only supports the first.

The marriage line ('mixed... marriage and partnerships') undersells what is actually one of the more scrutinised and, by all outside accounts, stable marriages of any modern head of state - together with Brigitte since the 1990s, married since 2007, a 24-year age gap that drew enormous public attention and that the marriage has simply outlasted. 'Mixed' is not wrong exactly, it is just vague enough that it can't be pinned down either way, which is the pattern for most of this page: safe enough to survive contact with the facts, specific enough to feel personal, but not specific enough to have told me anything about him before I already knew his story.

notes: Answered as Emmanuel Macron (b. 21 December 1977, Amiens; President of France since 2017), from the documented public record, having read the plain-words reading first. Judgement calls: A7/A8/A9/A10/A12/A13 (childhood health, danger before 8, grandparents' lifespans, and the closeness of his relationships with father/mother/siblings) are thinly documented in public biography - his maternal grandmother Germaine ('Manette') Noguès is the family figure most written about as a formative influence, not his parents directly, so 'close' for A10/A12/A13 is a best-fit default from the absence of any reported conflict rather than positive documented warmth, and A7-A9 are left 'unknown' rather than guessed. A14 'postgraduate' reflects ENA (Ecole nationale d'administration) completed after Sciences Po and a philosophy master's. A16/A17/A18 reflect the two-stage career (Rothschild investment banker 2008-2012, then civil servant/minister/president from 2012) - 'under_authority' was chosen because every post of his career, including the presidency, has been within an institution rather than a business of his own, which is also why C9 (own trade or business) was answered opt1 at only confidence 2: it barely applies to him. A20/A21/A22/A23 (foreign income, speculation, windfalls, debt) are answered from the absence of any reported scandal or disclosure to the contrary, which for a sitting French president is meaningfully documented territory (mandatory asset declarations), hence the higher confidence on C1 (debt, opt2, confidence 5) and C2 (illness, opt2, confidence 4). A28/A29 (children) reflect that Macron has no biological children; he has embraced Brigitte's three children and several grandchildren from her first marriage, but the question is about his own children, so 'none'/'na'. B2 was set to 'medium' rather than 'lean_tall' because his documented height (~173cm) is average for France, not tall, despite a lean/athletic build (boxing, tennis). C3/C4/C5/C6/C7/C8/C11 are all kept at confidence 3 because the public record on his inner life, minor health, mother, home comfort, money via marriage (Brigitte's family runs a chocolate business in Amiens), father, and his teenage boarding years at Lycee Henri-IV is suggestive but not deeply documented; C10 (learned/professional work has gone well) and C12 (immediate family has gone well) are the two confident calls (5 and 4) because they are the best-attested facts of his life. D1/D2 both point at the same single chapter (plain_reading, the only chapter shown) because it contains both a checkably wrong claim (debt flagged as an unusual negative when none is documented) and a checkably specific hit (political rivals flagged as unusual, which fits a president governing without a majority since 2024) - D3 also names plain_reading because most of the favourable content is generic enough to fit most accomplished people. D4 lists exactly the chapters not present in the supplied text, per the study protocol.
